My back thanks you for the push in class.

Joseph

Imran, you keep saying you'll start stretching and never do. Let me, your old boss Ramesh, tell you how I finally managed it at twenty-four.
I had a desk job in Chennai and a back like a plank. Every evening I promised myself I'd stretch “later.” Later never came. I'd think about it at night and feel lazy.
Then a colleague, an older lady named Thangam, told me, “Don't look for time. Tie it to something you already do.”
So I tied it to brushing my teeth. Toothbrush back in the cup, and I'd do five stretches right there at the sink. My wife thought I'd gone mad.
The first few days I had to remind myself. After two weeks, my hands put down the brush and my body just bent. I didn't have to think.
Thirty years later, I still do it every morning.
